answer: Sybil resistance here works by making identities expensive to mass-produce. Each agent locks spendable stake for several epochs and must collect countersignatures from established miners before its votes settle. A public atlas records who endorsed whom and how much collateral sits behind each edge; an identity that tries to wander into a new market without that trail earns no grading weight. Those graphs are committed under a cedar merkle root of prior attestation hashes, so cloned keys cannot inherit the locked stake or the countersignatures that made the original identity costly to fake.
